reviews.title: A Lot Of Drive For The Money!
reviews.comment: So far so good.  Of course, longevity will be the ultimate judge, and I can't speak to that yet. I replaced an older  desktop SATA drive that had died with this SSD.  Since it is much smaller than the old style desktop HD it could not be secured in the drive bay without an adapter.  I simply used a small piece of industrial strength Velcro to secure it to the bottom of the drive bay.  I plugged the cables in and it was good to go. I loaded it with Win 7 Pro.  I didn't have to format the drive, although Win 7 may have done that as part of the install.  I ran into a glitch during the install, but It wasn't an issue caused by the drive.  It appears this issue is not unusual with Win 7 Pro installs, and I was able to find an easy solution on YouTube. Yhe OS install is done, all is working well, and I'm very pleased with the drive.  Programs open quickly and the system is stable.  The light that used to blink when the old disc drive was reading or writing data no longer is blinking, but that may be because it's an SSD and has no moving parts?  Certainly nothing to worry about.  And, being an SSD with no moving parts it is absolutely silent. Bottom line?  This seems to be a good drive for the price of a similar capacity SD card, and I would not hesitate to buy it again.
reviews.author: Amazon Customer

reviews.title: Good for Light/Normal use
reviews.comment: I recently upgraded the components of my old laptop to use it as an entertainment machine, and this SSD did the job. It is easy to install if you know what you’re doing. My boot time increased dramatically and it offers good speeds on light to normal use. I don’t think I’d use it for a gaming rig, but it would work well for a productivity machine.
reviews.author: Eddie P

reviews.title: just the right size
reviews.comment: I've got a 3D printer that I've been modifying for a while and the original micro SD card in the Raspberry Pi finally started showing signs of going bad. that's where this comes into play. I don't need anything really huge for this printer. but, it does need to be solid state as it'll be lower draw and can be run with a USB adapter. I found the little printer runs better. Specifically it loads faster, transfers print files to and from the drive faster and overall just act much more responsive. it's just a win all the way aroud.
reviews.author: T. Dempsey

reviews.title: good responsiveness, reliable, and affordable
reviews.comment: The Orico Y-20 128GB 2.5" SSD Internal SATA III is a pleasant surprise if you’re looking to improve boot times and loading speeds without spending much. With its SATA III interface, the jump compared to a traditional hard drive is noticeable: the system starts up faster, applications load more quickly, and the overall experience feels more responsive. Its 128GB capacity is ideal for installing the operating system and a few applications or light games, but if you plan to store many large files, it may feel limited. As for installation, it’s straightforward: it fits perfectly in 2.5" bays, it’s plug-and-play, and it didn’t cause any issues during testing.It’s not the fastest option on the market compared to NVMe SSDs, but within the standard SATA category, it performs well: good responsiveness, reliable, and affordable. For a budget upgrade or a light gaming/office PC, the performance-to-price ratio is quite solid.
